original_question: Characterize exactly which graphs arise as visibility graphs of finite point sets in the plane, where two points are adjacent when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of the set.
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, Open Problem 2: "Characterize visibility graphs of point sets."
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended target very closely. It asks for an exact characterization problem, it is about visibility graphs of point sets in the plane, and its adjacency rule matches the paper's definition of mutual visibility: two points are adjacent when the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of the set.
missing_details: The paper is asking for a characterization of a class of undirected graphs G=(V,E), not just an informal description of point configurations.
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should state the existential quantifier explicitly: characterize those graphs G for which there exists a finite point set P⊂R^2.
The vertex-point correspondence should be explicit: there must be a bijection between V(G) and P.
Visibility is defined relative to the whole set P: two corresponding points are adjacent if and only if the segment joining them contains or passes through no other point of P.
No general-position assumption is present; collinearities are allowed, and such intervening points act as blockers.
The paper's name for this class is the point visibility graphs (or visibility graphs of point sets).
refined_question: Characterize the undirected graphs G that are point visibility graphs of finite point sets in the Euclidean plane; that is, determine necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a finite set P⊂R^2 and a bijection between V(G) and P such that two vertices of G are adjacent exactly when the line segment joining the corresponding points of P contains or passes through no other point of P.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's point-set visibility graph characterization problem, not the recognition problem (deciding for a given graph whether such a realization exists) and not the reconstruction problem (drawing a realizing point set). In Section 2.1 the paper explicitly defines the characterization problem and then states it as Open Problem 2. The draft's visibility rule is taken directly from the introduction's definition of mutual visibility and of the point visibility graph, so the closest paper-faithful sharpening is simply to make the graph variable, the existence quantifier, the bijection, and the ambient plane R^2 explicit.
